nodes.name: Electrodeposition of α-Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition of Co(OH)2 nanoarray on carbon cloth substrate in electrolyte containing Co(NO3)2, forming characteristic α-Co(OH)2 crystal structure with NO3- as interlayer anion.
nodes.source_text: Ru-Co(OH)2/CC was synthesized through a two-step procedure of electrodeposition followed by an ion-exchange process... Both Co(OH)2/CC and Ru–x–Co(OH)2/CC exhibit the characteristic crystal structure of α-Co(OH)2, with NO3- serving as the interlayer anion.

nodes.name: Ru Doping by Cation Exchange
nodes.procedure: Ion-exchange process by immersing electrodeposited Co(OH)2/CC in RuCl3 solution (concentrations: 0.2, 1, 5, and 10 mM) to form Ru-doped Co(OH)2/CC while preserving the α-Co(OH)2 nanosheet morphology and crystal structure (no Ru or RuO2 peaks observed).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show characteristic crystal structure of α-Co(OH)₂ for both Co(OH)₂/CC and Ru–x–Co(OH)₂/CC samples with NO₃⁻ as interlayer anion. No Ru species peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of Co(OH)₂/CC and Ru–x–Co(OH)₂/CC (x = 0.2, 1, 5, and 10...) are shown in Fig. 1a. Both Co(OH)₂/CC and Ru–x–Co(OH)₂/CC exhibit the characteristic crystal structure of α-Co(OH)₂, with NO₃⁻ serving as the interlayer anion. No diffraction peaks corresponding to Ru species (such as Ru or RuO₂) are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Ru–x–Co(OH)₂/CC show the uniform growth of densely arranged nanosheets across the CC substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of Ru–x–Co(OH)₂/CC (Fig. S1, ESI†) show the uniform growth of densely arranged nanosheets across the CC substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM analysis highlights the presence of ultrathin nanosheets, confirming that the Co(OH)₂ nanosheet morphology is preserved after the cation exchange process.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis (Fig. S2, ESI†) highlights the presence of ultrathin nanosheets, confirming that the Co(OH)₂ nanosheet morphology is preserved after the cation exchange process.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images reveal a new crystal lattice with a spacing of 0.242 nm, corresponding to CoO(OH) (100), in Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC after the 10th CV cycle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images revealed a new crystal lattice with a spacing of 0.242 nm, corresponding to CoO(OH) (100), in Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC after the 10th CV cycle in Ar-saturated 1 M KOH solution containing 2000 ppm NO₃⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows the absorption edge shifts to higher energy from pristine Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC to the 10th cycled sample, indicating an increase in Co oxidation state, with dynamic evolution during cycling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis at the Co K-edge was performed... Fig. 1e shows that the absorption edge shifts to a higher energy from the pristine Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC to the 10th cycled Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC, indicating an increase in the Co oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS shows two intensity maxima at approximately 5.0 Å⁻¹ and 7.1 Å⁻¹ attributed to Co–O and Co–Co contributions, with Co–O path slightly shifting to higher k-space after CV cycling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: WT contour plot of Ru-5-Co(OH)₂/CC before and after CV cycling exhibits two intensity maxima at approximately 5.0 Å⁻¹ and 7.1 Å⁻¹, attributed to the Co–O and Co–Co contributions, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy of Ru-Co(OH)₂/CC shows Co(OH)₂ peak at 527 cm⁻¹, emergence of CoO(OH) peak at 509 cm⁻¹ at -0.2 V vs RHE indicating partial oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺, and HNO peak at 1554 cm⁻¹ at -0.9 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Ru-Co(OH)₂/CC (Fig. 3f), the stretching vibration peak at 527 cm⁻¹, attributed to Co(OH)₂ was observed. At -0.2 V vs. RHE, a new peak at 509 cm⁻¹ corresponding to CoO(OH), appeared, suggesting partial oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺... Additionally, a peak at 1554 cm⁻¹, attributed to the N–O stretch of HNO, emerged as the potential shifted negatively to -0.9 V vs RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ EPR shows Ru-Co(OH)₂/CC exhibits significantly stronger DMPO–H signals than Co(OH)₂/CC after electrolysis, indicating enhanced hydrogen radical generation and rapid consumption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi EPR spectroscopy... As shown in Fig. 3d, after electrolysis in Ar-saturated 1 M KOH solution, Ru-Co(OH)₂/CC exhibits significantly stronger DMPO–H signals than Co(OH)₂/CC, indicating that Ru-Co(OH)₂/CC favors water dissociation and promotes the formation of active hydrogen necessary for protonation.
